cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Good morning, Kenton Festival box office. How can I help you?

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Oh, good morning. I’m coming to Kenton for a few days’ holiday next month, and a friend told me there’s a festival. She gave me this number to find out about it.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: That’s right, the festival begins on the 16th of May (Example) and goes on till the 19th.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Oh, that’s great. I’ll be there from the 15th till the 19th. So could you tell me the programme, please?

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Well, on the first day, there’s the opening ceremony, in the town centre. People start gathering around 2 o’clock, to get a good place to see from, and the events will start at 2.45 (Q1), and finish about 5.30.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: OK, thanks. I’ll make sure I get there early to get a good spot.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: The festival will be officially opened by the mayor. He’ll just speak for a few minutes, welcoming everyone to the festival. All the town councillors will be there, and of course lots of other people.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Right.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Then there’ll be a performance by a band (Q2). Most years we have a children’s choir, but this year the local army cadets offered to perform, and they’re very good.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Uhuh.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: After that, a community group from the town will perform a play they’ve written themselves, just a short one. It’s about Helen Tungate (Q3). I don’t know if you’ve heard of her?

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: I certainly have. She was a scientist years ago. (Q4)

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: That’s right. She was born in Kenton exactly 100 years ago, so we’re celebrating her centenary.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: I’m a biologist, so I’ve always been interested in her, I didn’t realise she came from Kenton.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Yes. Well, all that will take place in the afternoon, and later, as the sun sets, there’ll be a firework display. You should go to the park to watch, as you’ll get the best view from there, and the display takes place on the opposite side of the river (Q5). It’s always one of the most popular events in the festival.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Sounds great.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: And what’s happening on the other days?

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: There are several events that go on the whole time. For example, the students of the art college have produced a number of videos, all connected with relationships between children and their grandparents. (Q6)

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: That sounds interesting. It makes a change from children and parents, doesn’t it!

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Exactly. Because the art college is in use for classes, throughout the festival, the videos are being shown in Handsworth House. (Q7)

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: How do you spell the name?

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: H-A-N-D-S-W-O-R-T-H. Handsworth House. It’s close to the Town Hall.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Right.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Now let me see, what else can I tell you about?

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Are there any displays of ballet dancing? I’m particularly interested in that as I do it as a hobby.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: There isn’t any ballet, I’m afraid, but there’ll be a demonstration of traditional dances from all round the country. (Q8)

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Oh, that’d be nice. Where’s that being held?

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: It’s in the market in the town centre - the outdoor one, not the covered market (Q9). And it’s on at 2 and 5 every afternoon of the festival, apart from the first day.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Lovely. I’m interested in all kinds of dancing, so I’m sure I’ll enjoy that!

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Mmm. I’m sure you will.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: And I’d really like to go to some concerts, if there are any.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Yes, there are several. Three performed by professionals, and one by local children.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: And where is it being held?

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: It’s in the library, which is in Part Street. On the 18th, at 6.30 in the evening.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: I presume I’ll need tickets for that.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Yes, you can book online, or you can buy them when you arrive in Kenton, either at the festival box office, or from any shops displaying our logo in the windows. (Q10)

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Well, I think that’ll keep me busy for the whole of my stay in Kenton. Thank you so much for all your help.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: You’re welcome. I hope you enjoy your stay.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Thank you. Goodbye.
